claims.text: The system is a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy coating on a single-crystal Cu substrate.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating is 21 Å thick.
The Cu substrate has dimensions of 100 Å × 100 Å × 55 Å.
The coating and Cu substrate initially have FCC structures oriented along [100], [010], and [001].
The proposed temperature intervention compares tests at 300 K, 600 K, 900 K, and 1200 K.
The virtual indenter is pressed at 10 m/s to a depth of 30 Å over 300 ps and unloaded at the same speed over 300 ps.
The coating retains an ordered FCC lattice from 300 K through 600 K.
Dislocation density remains stable between 300 K and 600 K.
Temperatures above approximately 900 K induce rapid lattice disorder.
Temperatures above approximately 900 K significantly reduce dislocation density.
Temperatures above approximately 900 K increase the HCP atom fraction.
Around 600 K, a modest reduction in dislocation density can increase the elastic modulus.
Above 900 K, deformation shifts from stacking-fault-mediated behavior to predominantly disordered-lattice mechanisms.
High-temperature lattice disorder sharply reduces hardness and elastic modulus.
Hardness and wear resistance remain relatively stable from 300 K to 600 K.
Wear resistance and hardness decrease sharply above approximately 900 K.
Friction coefficient and tangential force increase above approximately 900 K.
Friction coefficient and tangential force exhibit significant fluctuations above approximately 900 K.
Higher dislocation density at the 300 K baseline ensures stable wear resistance.
A critical transition near 900 K separates dislocation-governed deformation from deformation dominated by lattice disorder and HCP formation.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator says dislocation density is stable throughout 300–600 K, whereas the mechanism invokes a modest reduction in dislocation density around 600 K. These statements require clarification about whether the change at 600 K is negligible or mechanistically meaningful.
